summary: A man was arrested at Fairbanks on Oct. 12 after a reported robbery at a sporting goods shop, on offences police recorded as robbery in the first degree, misconduct involving a weapon in the third degree and assault in the third degree; no court file has been opened and no charge class is stated. The Alaska Court System's weekly criminal charges report, run-stamped 9:01 p.m. Oct. 12, lists 43 Fairbanks cases, 4 at Nenana, 2 at Delta Junction and none at Healy for the window Oct. 6 to Oct. 12, and places two further Fairbanks cases under Sunday, Oct. 11, a day the previous run printed with three; one of the two carries a concealed-weapon count corresponding to a traffic stop on Oct. 8. A grand jury indicted the Delta Junction arson case 4DJ-26-00060CR on Oct. 9, and the arson count is now recorded on the file as a Class B felony. The Nenana case 4NE-26-00096CR is indicted on a Class B felony burglary count in place of an earlier Class C felony charge. Six Fairbanks cases were filed on Monday, three of their counts recorded as domestic violence related. Troopers reported two further incidents on Oct. 12 at North Pole and one at Fairbanks early on Oct. 13. Counts in the filings table are the weekly report's own counts for its stated window, which closes at 9 p.m. and is short of its own last filing day; the court has also opened eight Fairbanks case numbers that the report does not print, and prints one number, 4FA-26-02024CR, that the public case-number search returns no record for. The criminal dispositions report has not refreshed since Oct. 12.

entries.title: Man arrested after a reported robbery at a Fairbanks sporting goods shop; no court file has been opened
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, incident AK26101825, posted at 6:16 p.m. on Oct. 12, records that at 13:46 on Oct. 12 troopers responded to Beaver Sports in Fairbanks for a reported robbery, that the investigation determined that Daniel Schwietert, 25, of Fairbanks committed the crimes of robbery in the first degree, misconduct involving a weapon in the third degree and assault in the third degree, and that he was placed under arrest and remanded to the Fairbanks Correctional Center.

No court file under that name corresponds to the incident. A CourtView name search limited to Sept. 1 to Oct. 13, 2026 returns no records, and an unfiltered search returns no criminal case more recent than one filed in 2025. The three offences above are charges recorded by police, not counts on a court record, and no charge class is stated because none appears on any court file. He is arrested, not charged on a court record and not convicted.

entries.title: Two further Fairbanks cases appear on the weekly report under Sunday, Oct. 11, one of them a concealed-weapon count
body: The Alaska Court System's weekly criminal charges report, run-stamped 9:01 p.m. on Oct. 12, lists five Fairbanks cases under Sunday, Oct. 11. The run before it, stamped 9:00 p.m. on Oct. 11, listed three. The two additional cases are 4FA-26-02069CR and 4FA-26-02070CR, both of which carry a file date of Oct. 11 in CourtView.

4FA-26-02069CR, against Michael Devin Lamoreaux, carries one count: misconduct involving weapons in the fifth degree, carrying a concealed weapon and failing to inform an officer, AS 11.61.220(a)(1)(A)(i), a Class B misdemeanour, offence-dated Oct. 8 at Fairbanks. The case judge is Seekins and an arraignment is calendared for Nov. 17. The count corresponds to the concealed-weapon charge police recorded after a traffic stop on Van Horn Road on Oct. 8.

4FA-26-02070CR, against Kimberly Jonette Leitzel, carries two counts, both offence-dated Oct. 10 at Fairbanks: driving under the influence with a blood alcohol content of .08 per cent or more, AS 28.35.030(a)(2), a Class A misdemeanour; and assault in the fourth degree, cause fear of injury, AS 11.41.230(a)(3), a Class A misdemeanour. The case judge is Bahr. No event is calendared on the file. Both are charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Delta Junction arson case indicted, with the arson count recorded on the file as a Class B felony
body: Alaska CourtView records that a grand jury returned an indictment in 4DJ-26-00060CR, State of Alaska against Nicholas Gene Dollar, on Oct. 9, 2026, with docket entries reading Indictment Filed in Open Court and Log Notes: Grand Jury Log Notes. Both counts are now recorded as indicted counts.

Count 1 is arson in the second degree, AS 11.46.410, recorded on the file as a Class B felony. Count 2 is criminal mischief in the fourth degree, AS 11.46.484(a)(1), a Class A misdemeanour. Both counts are offence-dated Oct. 1 at Delta Junction and both are recorded as domestic violence related.

An arraignment is calendared for Oct. 14 at the Fairbanks courthouse, an omnibus hearing in Superior Court for Nov. 5 and a trial week for Nov. 23. A bail hearing was logged on Oct. 12. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: A further count appears on the 1993 Fairbanks homicide file after a change of plea
body: Alaska CourtView records four counts on 4FA-25-02251CR, State of Alaska against Christopher M. Popps, all recorded as indicted counts. Counts 1 and 2 are murder in the second degree, AS 11.41.110(a)(2) and AS 11.41.110(a)(1), unclassified felonies. Count 3 is AS 11.41.130, a Class B felony. Count 4 is recorded as a charging document pending or not filed, with no degree of offence. The offences are dated Nov. 22, 1993 at Fairbanks.

The docket records a change of plea heard on Oct. 2, an order for a presentence report dated Oct. 5 and a criminal deficiency memo dated Oct. 12. A scheduled trial week of Oct. 12 is recorded as vacated. Sentencing in Superior Court is calendared for March 23, 2027 before Judge Temple. Earlier editions of this report recorded that the reduced count a newspaper column had described did not appear on the file; it appears as count 3.

entries.title: Nenana case indicted on a Class B felony burglary count after an earlier Class C felony charge
body: Alaska CourtView records 4NE-26-00096CR, State of Alaska against Krista Marie Zappone, as indicted, with docket entries dated Oct. 6 reading Indictment Filed in Superior Court, Jurisdiction Transferred to Superior Court; Log Notes: Grand Jury Returns; and Information Adding Misdemeanor Count to Indictment.

The indicted count is burglary in the first degree, in a dwelling, AS 11.46.300(a)(1), a Class B felony. The original charge on the same count is recorded as burglary in the second degree, AS 11.46.310, a Class C felony. The file also carries criminal trespass in the first degree, in a dwelling, AS 11.46.320(a)(2), a Class A misdemeanour; theft in the fourth degree, AS 11.46.150(a), a Class B misdemeanour; and two counts of violating conditions of release, AS 11.56.757(a), Class B misdemeanours. All counts are offence-dated Sept. 25, 2026. The offence locations recorded on the file are Denali National Park and Cantwell; the case is filed at the Nenana court and heard at the Fairbanks courthouse.

The file states a total of six party charges and displays five; no charge numbered 5 is rendered. An arraignment is calendared for Oct. 14 at Fairbanks, a calendar call for Nov. 17 and a trial week for Nov. 30. She is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Arrest at North Pole for a probation violation after a reported disturbance
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, incident AK26101732, posted at 5:01 p.m. on Oct. 12, records that troopers responded to a residence in North Pole for a report of a disturbance and contacted Kelly Hoffman, 44, of North Pole; that it was determined she had been drinking alcohol; that she is on probation and ordered not to consume, possess or purchase alcohol; and that she was arrested and remanded to the Fairbanks Correctional Center for a probation violation.

The only criminal court file under that name, 4FA-25-00781CR, is recorded as closed. It was filed in April 2025 on two Class A misdemeanour counts, driving under the influence and refusing to submit to a chemical test, and its docket carries an order dated Sept. 4, 2026 reading Do Not Possess, Consume, or Purchase Alcohol. No docket entry on that file records an arrest on Oct. 12 and no new case has been opened under the name on the record as read. She is arrested, not convicted of anything arising from Oct. 12.

entries.title: Six Fairbanks cases filed on Monday, including three domestic violence counts and a protective order violation
body: 4FA-26-02071CR, against Dakota Rose Griffin, carries three counts, all offence-dated Oct. 11 at Fairbanks and all recorded as domestic violence related: criminal mischief in the fifth degree, tampering with property, AS 11.46.486(a)(1), a Class B misdemeanour; assault in the fourth degree, recklessly injure, AS 11.41.230(a)(1), a Class A misdemeanour; and assault when a child is present, AS 11.41.240(a), a Class A misdemeanour. An arraignment was held on Oct. 12 and a pre-trial conference is calendared for Nov. 19.

4FA-26-02074CR, against Curtis Ian McDonald Jr, carries violating a domestic violence protective order, AS 11.56.740(a)(1), a Class A misdemeanour recorded as domestic violence related, and violating conditions of release, AS 11.56.757(a), a Class B misdemeanour. Both counts are offence-dated Sept. 25 at Fairbanks. A summons was requested and no event is calendared.

4FA-26-02072CR, against Ishi Sarten, carries criminal trespass in the second degree, upon premises, AS 11.46.330(a)(1), a Class B misdemeanour, offence-dated Oct. 11. It is the court file for a Fairbanks Police Department bulletin entry recording an arrest at 13:57 on Oct. 11 at the 1300 block of South University Avenue on two charges; the file carries the trespass count only.

4FA-26-02073CR, against Marshall Jordan Rayden Haworth, carries theft in the fourth degree, under $250, AS 11.46.150(a), a Class B misdemeanour, offence-dated Oct. 11. 4FA-26-02075CR, against Frederick Mayo, and 4FA-26-02076CR, against Terrance Fields, each carry one count of theft in the fourth degree, AS 11.46.150(a), a Class B misdemeanour, both offence-dated Sept. 9 at Fairbanks. All are charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Man taken into custody for disorderly conduct in Fairbanks about an hour after being warned at the same location
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, incident AK26101950, posted at 1:30 a.m. on Oct. 13, records that at about 11:43 p.m. on Oct. 12 troopers responded to multiple calls of a male yelling in the street and banging on doors; that this followed a response to the same location at about 10:39 p.m. at which the male was given a disorderly conduct warning; and that he was placed into custody without further incident for disorderly conduct. The release names no one and no court file corresponding to it was found on the record as read.

entries.title: Two dirt bikes reported stolen at North Pole, both recovered
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, incident AK26101389, posted at 6:14 a.m. on Oct. 12, records that at about 0600 on Oct. 11 troopers responded to the area of Secluded Drive in North Pole for the theft of two dirt bikes; that one was recovered on Secluded Drive and one was later recovered by North Pole Police after a driver fled a traffic stop; and that the investigation continues. No arrest and no charge are stated.

entries.title: Two Fairbanks Police arrest entries appear on earlier dates, matching two court files that carried no charge
body: The Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin for Oct. 10 now carries three entries where it carried two. The additional entry, case 26003108, records an arrest at 02:53 on Oct. 10 at the 400 block of the Johansen Expressway ramp to College Road on charges of driving under the influence and refusing to submit to a chemical test. The name corresponds to the defendant on court file 4FA-26-02059CR.

The bulletin for Oct. 9 now carries six entries where it carried five. The additional entry, case 26003099, records an arrest at 15:13 on Oct. 9 at the 300 block of the Johansen Expressway at Alaska Railroad Depot Road on a charge of disorderly conduct, creating a hazardous condition. The name corresponds to the defendant on court file 4FA-26-02058CR; the bulletin and the court file spell the surname differently.

Both court files are recorded as charging document pending or not filed with no degree of offence, so no charge class is stated for either. The charges above are charges recorded by police. Both are arrested, not convicted.

entries.title: Five Fairbanks files that carried no docket entry at all have each gained a release order dated Oct. 12
body: Five Fairbanks criminal files that had carried no docket entry of any kind each now carry one row, an Order and Conditions - Release per Schedule dated Oct. 12: 4FA-26-02052CR, 4FA-26-02058CR, 4FA-26-02059CR, 4FA-26-02060CR and 4FA-26-02066CR. Four of the five carry an arraignment calendared for Oct. 16 at the Fairbanks courthouse.

All five remain recorded as charging document pending or not filed, with no degree of offence. A release order is not a charging document, and no charge class is stated for any of the five because none appears on any of the files. Eleven Fairbanks-area files carry no charging document at the time of reading, the oldest of them filed twenty-four days ago.

entries.title: One case filed at Delta Junction on Monday
body: 4DJ-26-00063CR, State of Alaska against Tracie Davis, was filed on Oct. 12 carrying one count of permitting an unauthorised person to drive, AS 28.15.281(b), recorded as a misdemeanour not classified, offence-dated Jun. 5, 2026 at Delta Junction. The case judge is Young. She is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Weekly charges report: 43 Fairbanks cases, 4 at Nenana, 2 at Delta Junction, none at Healy
body: The Alaska Court System's weekly criminal charges report carries the stamp Report Run Date: 10/12/2026 9:01 pm and the window 10/6/2026 to 10/12/2026, across 62 pages. Read in full for the four Interior court prefixes, it lists 43 cases at Fairbanks, 4 at Nenana, 2 at Delta Junction and no Healy section at all.

Fairbanks cases by filing day: three on Oct. 6, six on Oct. 7, seven on Oct. 8, eight on Oct. 9, eight on Oct. 10, five on Oct. 11 and six on Oct. 12. The five under Oct. 11 include two that were not in the previous run. The Nenana cases are 4NE-26-00100CR filed Oct. 7, 4NE-26-00101CR and 4NE-26-00102CR filed Oct. 8 and 4NE-26-00103CR filed Oct. 10, unchanged in membership from the previous run; Nenana added no case on Oct. 11 or Oct. 12. The Delta Junction cases are 4DJ-26-00062CR filed Oct. 9 and 4DJ-26-00063CR filed Oct. 12.

The report's window closes at 9 p.m. and is therefore short of its own last filing day. Eight Fairbanks case numbers between 4FA-26-02042CR and 4FA-26-02049CR, opened on Oct. 8 and each styled State of Alaska vs. Grand Jury with no degree of offence, appear in no run of this report. A twelfth Fairbanks-area case number the report prints, 4FA-26-02024CR under Oct. 6, returns no record on the public case-number search; eleven others have done so on each of the last five days.

entries.title: The criminal dispositions report has not refreshed since Oct. 12
body: The Alaska Court System's criminal cases disposed report carries the footer stamp Data updated 10/12/2026 at 4:00 am, the same stamp as the previous reading, and the header Case Closed Between: 9/1/2026 to 10/12/2026. The file runs to 237 pages and carries 182 distinct Fairbanks case numbers, 11 at Nenana, 6 at Delta Junction and none at Healy, every figure identical to the previous reading. Freshness is taken from the footer stamp rather than the page count. No conclusion is drawn from an unrefreshed file about what the court has closed since Oct. 12.
